Carfax records a February 2016 'minor damage' entry to the left/left-front; no invoices, no body-shop name, no panel list, no paint-depth readings offered. A pre-sale paint correction and ceramic coating were performed, which can mask panel-to-panel differences.

documentation.rationale: What exists is a Carfax summary (12 service entries, 3 owners, a 2016 left-front damage entry) plus seller prose. There is no invoice folder, no Porsche or independent service file, no water-pump or brake-fluid record, no clutch/DMF history, no DME over-rev report, no borescope, and no repair documentation for the disclosed damage. Carfax line items are third-hand references, not receipts, and the seller has left the highest-value documentation requests in the comments unanswered.

condition.rationale: Presentation is genuinely good: photos show straight dark blue paint after a paint correction and ceramic coating, clean pebble-gray leather with no obvious bolster wear, tidy 20" wheels, and a dry-looking rear underbody with no rust. Positives on record: headlights replaced 2024 (a $2k+ item pre-paid), plugs and serpentine belt 2022, fresh oil. Against that, at 78k miles and 12 years the water pump, brake fluid, coolant, AGM battery, clutch/DMF and PASM/damper condition are all undocumented, the tires are non-N-spec Nittos of unknown age, the left-front was damaged in 2016 with no repair record, and the single most catastrophic risk on this engine (bore scoring) has no borescope or consumption evidence at all.

price_value.rationale: At the current $17,500 no-reserve bid this is well under market for a 981 manual, which is the configuration the market pays a premium for. Realistically it will run higher; a base 2.7 with 78k miles, a Carfax damage entry and undocumented aftermarket exhaust should trade below a clean documented car, so value stays good up to roughly $23k hammer (~$24.2k with BaT fee) and evaporates as it approaches the mid-$20s where documented cars and Boxster S examples appear. Add ~$1,500 transport and $1,600-$2,600 of known tire work and the all-in crowds Jason's $27,000 max quickly.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper the 981 manual is exactly right — last NA mid-engine Porsche roadster, no IMS, superb on Highway 1 and the Laureles Grade, and a manual, which the buyer requires. But the keeper case rests on documentation and originality, and this car is the undocumented, damage-reported, modified-exhaust version of the recipe. It is also the cash-heavier path at a moment when the strategy calls for preserving cash against the 335i's exit; it does not solve the bridge problem, it is a discretionary keeper purchase.

logistics.rationale: North Royalton, Ohio is a fly-out-and-drive-home car, which is a cost item and fine in principle — but the auction ends 2026-09-09, roughly three days out, which is a tight window to book a Cleveland-area Porsche specialist for a borescope, DME pull and cooling pressure test, and the dealer has not responded to simpler requests. The larger logistics issue is California: an out-of-state 2014 with unidentified aftermarket exhaust must pass a smog inspection with visual catalyst verification, and nobody has confirmed the cats are intact.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Dark Blue Metallic over Pebble/Agate Gray with a blue top, Sport seats, SportDesign wheel, bi-xenon PDLS and 20" Carrera S wheels is a genuinely handsome, non-default spec, and a manual open-top flat-six in Carmel is close to ideal. Points off because it is the 2.7 base without Sport Chrono or PSE, and the fake-S dual central exhaust is exactly the kind of 'appear to be something it isn't' modification that grates on an originality-minded owner and shaves resale.

evidence.mission_note: As a future_keeper this is the right car in the wrong condition of evidence: a genuine 981 manual in an attractive spec, but with a damage entry, undocumented aftermarket exhaust, and none of the model-critical engine or top evidence supplied. It does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem — a two-seat convertible will not replace the 335i's daily role — so it is a discretionary keeper buy that competes directly with the cash needed for the bridge car.
evidence.rationale: Verdict driver: the evidence file is thin on exactly the items that decide whether a 78k-mile 9A1 is a bargain or a $20,000 mistake. No borescope, no DME over-rev report (and the DME itself was replaced in 2021, per Carfax, which may have truncated that history), no water-pump or brake-fluid record, and no full top-cycle video despite a bidder asking for one on September 4. Carfax does establish a February 2016 'minor damage' event to the left and left-front, and no repair documentation is offered — while a fresh paint correction and ceramic coating have just been applied over the area. The 'aftermarket exhaust components' are the second material issue: the rear photo shows S-style dual central outlets on a base 2.7 and the underside photo shows a non-factory rear section, but two commenters have asked whether cats or headers are involved and the seller has answered neither, which is a live California smog-and-registration question, not a cosmetic quibble. On the positive side the car photographs well — straight dark blue panels, clean Pebble Gray leather with no visible bolster wear, a dry rust-free rear underbody — and it carries real pre-paid value in the March 2024 headlight replacement plus 2022 plugs and serpentine belt. The tires are non-N-spec Nittos of unstated age, so budget a set plus alignment as known work, on top of $3,200-$5,800 of first-year catch-up for cooling, fluids, battery and top service. At $17,500 no reserve it is cheap; at the $22k-$28k range this configuration usually reaches, the discount for the damage entry and the fake-S exhaust disappears and the buyer is paying near-documented-car money for an undocumented car. Everything hinges on getting a specialist onto it in the three days remaining.
evidence.next_action: Today, book a Porsche specialist near North Royalton, OH for a pre-close PPI with borescope of all six cylinders, DME over-rev/PIWIS pull, cooling pressure test, lift photos confirming both catalytic converters, and three full top cycles — and post the exhaust and DME questions publicly in the BaT comments so a non-answer is on the record before bidding.
